title: Characterizing Selective Refusal Bias in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Selective refusal bias in safety guardrails, specifically measuring the variation in refusal rates for toxic prompts targeting different religious groups.
findings: All models tested showed the highest refusal rates for toxic prompts targeting Jews and Muslims, indicating stronger safety protections for these groups. Conversely, they exhibited the lowest refusal rates for prompts targeting Taoists, Atheists, and Christians, suggesting a bias where models are more likely to comply with generating harmful content against these latter groups.
